prompt: A manufacturer's new plant runs at 55% of capacity a year after opening. Demand forecasts had assumed 85%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The plant runs at 55% of capacity against an 85% forecast.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: It could be demand, production problems, staffing, pricing or the forecast itself.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: The forecasting team got it wrong, and that is the only reason.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: Demand likely fell short of forecast, perhaps because the forecast assumed new customers who didn't come.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare forecast and actual orders by customer.

explanation: Low utilization means demand or production fell short. Orders by customer against forecast tells which.
